validity_note: Laliberte (2009) aqueous-electrolyte correlation for Na2SO4-water, density and viscosity. Tabulated for 2-14 wt% over 20-60 degC. Sodium sulfate has an unusual solubility curve that collapses as it cools: stable saturation is only about 16 wt% Na2SO4 at 20 degC (as the decahydrate, Glauber's salt) and falls steeply below that, so the 20 degC floor and 14 wt% ceiling keep the whole table below saturation. Heat capacity is not tabulated: the correlation's Na2SO4 heat-capacity data begins at 25 degC, above this table's floor, so it is omitted rather than extrapolated. Concentrations are anhydrous Na2SO4; the decahydrate (Glauber's salt) is 44% Na2SO4 by mass. Values are for preliminary design; verify against vendor data for critical service.
